## Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (“the 2024 Act”)

## 13A.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 13A.1] A party who relies on a CMA breach decision (which has the same meaning as in section 102(5) of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024), must state that in their statement of case, and must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 13A.1] identify the CMA breach decision; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > 13A.1] indicate whether the CMA breach decision is final (in accordance with section 102(2) of the 2024 Act)

## Human Rights

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] 14.1 A party who relies on any provision of or right arising under the Human Rights Act 1998 or seeks a remedy under that Act must state that fact in their statement of case, and must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (a) give details of the Convention right infringed and details of the infringement;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (b) specify the relief sought;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (c) state if the relief sought includes—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (i) a declaration of incompatibility under section 4 if that Act, or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (ii) damages in respect of a judicial act to which section 9(3) of that Act applies;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (d) where the relief sought includes a declaration of incompatibility, give details of the legislative provision and the alleged incompatibility;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (e) where the claim is founded on a finding of unlawfulness by another court or tribunal, give details of the finding; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (f) where the claim is founded on a judicial act alleged to have infringed a Convention right of the party as provided by section 9 of the Human Rights Act 1998, the judicial act complained of and the court or tribunal that made it. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (Practice Direction 19A provides for notice to be given and parties joined in the circumstances referred to in (c), (d) and (f).)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] 14.2 A party seeking to amend a statement of case to include the matters referred to in paragraph 14.1 must, unless the court orders otherwise, do so as soon as possible. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] (Part 17 provides for the amendment of a statement of case.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 16 – STATEMENTS OF CASE > Human Rights] Updated: Sunday, 1 October 2023
